		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Critical Accounting Policies</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Critical Accounting Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The preparation of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> in conformity with </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">GAAP</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> requires management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, and disclosure of contingent gains and losses at the date of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the period. We base our judgments, estimates and assumptions on historical experience and various other factors that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ materially from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions. We evaluate our judgments, estimates and assumptions on a regular basis and make changes accordingly. We believe that the judgments, estimates and assumptions involved in the accounting for revenue recognition, income taxes, the allowance for doubtful accounts receivable, stock-based compensation, useful lives of intangible assets and intangible asset impairment, goodwill impairment, acquisition accounting</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> including the fair value of contingent acquisition consideration</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, and contingencies have the greatest potential impact on our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, so we consider these to be our critical accounting policies. Below we discuss the critical accounting estimates associated with these policies. For further information on our critical accounting policies, see Note </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to our consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> on Form 10-K</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Online advertising is the sale of advertising, sponsorships, hyperlinks, and lead generation within our online network through our owned and operated sites, such as </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">CreditCards.com,</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Bankrate.com </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Caring.com</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> The </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">print publishing and licensing</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> business is primarily engaged in the sale of advertising</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, mortgage and interest rate tables</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and licensing of research information.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Consumer Inquiry Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">In the credit card segment, we deliver consumer inquiries as a click or phone call to our advertisers and primarily recognize revenue on a per-completed and approved application basis. We also have some card issuer agreements which recognize revenue on a per-completed application basis. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">In the banking segment, we deliver consumer inquiries in the form of clicks and calls and recognize revenue monthly based on the number of clicks and calls at a cost-per-click/call for our mortgage and deposit and other banking products. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">In the senior care vertical we deliver consumer inquiries to contracting senior care communities after qualifying the inquiries in our call center and matching them to a number of suitable communities. We recognize revenue for each consumer who actually moves into a community for which we provided the initial referral. We also deliver consumer leads to participating in-home care providers, for which we receive fees on a per-lead basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We have also entered into revenue sharing arrangements with our vertical content and affiliate partners based on the revenue earned from their consumer inquiries.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue is recorded at gross amounts and partnership and affiliate payments are recorded in cost of revenue, pursuant to the provisions of Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) Topic 605-45, Reporting Revenue Gross as a Principal versus Net as an Agent.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Display Advertising Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Display advertising sales are invoiced monthly at amounts based on specific contract terms</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, which are</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> predominantly based on the number of impressions delivered to the advertiser.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Print Publishing and Licensing Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We charge for placement in the mortgage and interest rate table for print publication. Advertising revenue is recognized when the rate tables run in a publication. Revenue from the sale of research information is recognized ratably over the contract period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We account for share-based compensation in accordance with ASC&nbsp;718, Compensation&#x2014;Stock Compensation. Under the fair value recognition provisions of ASC&nbsp;718, share-based compensation cost is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">For awards with performance conditions, the probable outcomes of the performance conditions are assessed and if the conditions are determined as not probable to be achieved, no compensation cost will be recognized. If it is determined that the conditions are probable to be achieved, the related stock-based compensation expense is recognized over the requisite service period of the related awards. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The valuation provisions of ASC&nbsp;718 apply to new grants and to grants that are subsequently modified. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Acquisition Accounting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">have acquired </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">numerous businesses and websites</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> The acquisition method of accounting requires companies to assign values to assets and liabilities acquired based upon their fair values. In most instances, there is not a readily defined or listed market price for individual assets and liabilities acquired in connection with a business, including intangible assets. The determination of fair value for assets and liabilities in many instances requires a high degree of estimation. The valuation of intangibles assets, in particular, is very subjective. We generally use internal cash flow models. The use of different valuation techniques and assumptions can change the amounts and useful lives assigned to the assets and liabilities acquired, including goodwill and other intangible assets and related amortization expense. We applied ASC 805, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Business Combinations</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">to all business combinations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Goodwill Impairment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The Company records the excess of purchase price over the fair value of the net tangible and identified intangible assets acquired as goodwill. The goodwill is tested for impairment annually, as well as when an event, or change in circumstances, indicates impairment may have occurred. In accordance with ASC 350, Intangibles-Goodwill and Other, we first assess qualitative factors to determine whether the existence of events or circumstances leads to a determination that it is more likely than not (a likelihood of more than 50%) that the fair value of our reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. We perform this assessment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> at the reporting unit level</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> annually on October 1st, or more frequently if facts and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> circumstances warrant a review</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. If after assessing the qualitative factors we determine that it is not more likely than not that the fair value of the reporting unit is less than the carrying value</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> then we conclude that we have no goodwill impairment and no further testing is performed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> otherwise, we proceed to the two-step process. The first step under the two</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">-</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">step process is to compare the fair value of the reporting unit to its carrying value. If the fair value exceeds the carrying value, goodwill is not impaired and no further testing is performed. The reporting unit fair values are determined by using a weighted valuation approach among three different valuation methodologies consisting of an income approach and a market approach</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> which is made up of the &#x2018;guideline company method&#x2019; and the &#x2018;reference transaction method&#x2019;. The second step is performed if the carrying value exceeds the fair value. The implied fair value of the reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill must be determined and compared to the carrying value of the goodwill. If the carrying value of a reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill exceeds its implied </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">fair </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">value, an impairment loss equal to the difference will be recorded. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The Company followed the guidance in ASC 350-20-35 and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">performed the annual impairment test of goodwill as of October 1, 2016. In performing that test, it was noted that the carrying value of the Senior Care reporting unit exceeded its fair value. As a result, the second step was required to be performed. The implied fair value of goodwill was determined in the same manner as the amount of goodwill recognized in a business combination. We have determined the fair value of the reporting unit using the income and market approaches. We also determined the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">fair value of developed technology, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">domain names</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and customer relationships, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">using </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">relevant market related data. We recorded </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$4.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million for impairment of goodwill of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior Care reporting unit for the year ended December 31, 2016.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">During 2016, management revised the strategy of its Quizzle reporting unit to focus its technology resources primarily on enhancing the user experience of the products and services provided by the Banking segment through greater personalization, and realigned its management reporting structure by integrating </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Quizzle operations</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> into the Banking </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. Management determined that the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">revised strategy, reporting structure and the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">performance of initiatives utilizing Quizzle resources, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">each </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">represented triggering event</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> for impairment testing at the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">pre-realigned </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Quizzle reporting unit. As a result we completed Step 1 analysis of goodwill during the third quarter</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> 2016, which indicated that the fair value was lower than the reporting unit&#x2019;s carrying value, and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">recorded an estimated goodwill impairment of $4.2 million in the third quarter of 2016. During the fourth quarter 2016, we </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">completed Step 2 of the analysis</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">recording an additional goodwill impairment of $2.4 million for the pre-realigned Quizzle reporting unit for the year ended December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. The impairment amount was determined using the income and market approaches, and was based on a number of factors including the estimated fair value of developed technology, trademarks and customer relationships, as well as relevant market related data. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">During the second quarter 2016, management noted that the operating results of its Banking reporting unit had begun to track below plan, primarily due to macroeconomic trends impacting its deposit and display advertising businesses. This triggering event resulted in impairment testing as of June 30, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> determined using the income and market approaches</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. It was concluded that the reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill was impaired and we recorded</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> $25.0 million impairment of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">its </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">goodwill </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">second quarter of 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. The Banking reporting unit was tested for impairment again during our annual assessment and it was concluded that no impairment had occurred. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">During 2015, it was determined that a triggering event had occurred in our former Insurance business unit. We recorded a $35.0 million charge for the impairment of goodwill within our Insurance </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting unit </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">resulting from the difference between the net book value of the business segment and the estimated fair value of the business. During the annual goodwill impairment testing, on October 1, 2015, we performed the assessment for all reporting units, including Step 2 testing for the Insurance </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">unit, and concluded that there was no impairment of goodwill</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> including any further impairment of the Insurance </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">unit. During the fourth quarter 2015, the Insurance business was disposed and as such, the results of the business are presented as</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> discontinued operation for all periods presented.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets including intangible assets with finite lives</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">ASC 360, Property, Plant and Equipment, requires that long-lived assets including intangible assets with finite lives be amortized over their estimated useful life and reviewed for impairment. We continually monitor events and changes in circumstances that could indicate carrying amounts of our long-lived assets including intangible assets with finite lives may not be recoverable. When such events or changes in circumstances occur, we assess the recoverability of such assets by determining whether the carrying value will be recovered through the undiscounted expected future cash flows. If the future undiscounted cash flows are less than the carrying amount of such assets, we recognize an impairment loss based on the excess of the carrying amount over the fair value of the assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">As noted above, d</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">uring the third quarter 2016, management realigned its management reporting structure by integrating the Quizzle operations into the Banking </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">revised the strategy of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Quizzle reporting unit to focus its technology resources primarily on enhancing the user experience of the products and services provided by the Banking segment t</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">hrough greater personalization. T</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">hese changes, along with </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">a change in the estimated useful life of Quizzle&#x2019;s developed technology intangible asset and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the performance of initiatives utilizing Quizzle resources, represented a triggering event for impairment testing at the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">pre-realigned </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Quizzle reporting unit. It was determined that the intangible assets of our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">pre-realigned </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Quizzle </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">reporting</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> unit were impaired and we recorded </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">a $7.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> impairment to the pre-realigned Quizzle reporting unit intangible assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We performed impairment evaluations in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> 2015 and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, and concluded that there was no impairment of long</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">-</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">lived assets including intangible assets with finite lives.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We maintain an allowance for doubtful accounts for estimated losses resulting from the inability or unwillingness of our customers to make required payments. We look at historical write-offs and sales growth when determining the adequacy of the allowance. This estimate is inherently subjective because our estimates may be revised as more information becomes available. Should the financial condition of our customers deteriorate, resulting in an impairment of their ability to make payments, or if the level of accounts receivable increases, the need for possible additional allowances may be necessary. Any additions to the allowance for doubtful accounts are recorded as bad debt expense and included in general and administrative expenses. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Contingencies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">As discussed in Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to our consolidated financial statements, included elsewhere in this Annual Report</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> on Form 10-K</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, various legal proceedings are pending against us. We record provisions in the consolidated financial statements for pending litigation when we determine that an unfavorable outcome is probable and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. Except as discussed in Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, at the present time, while it is reasonably possible that an unfavorable outcome in a case may occur, (i) management has concluded that it is not probable that a loss has been incurred; (ii) management is unable to estimate the possible loss or range of loss that could result from an unfavorable outcome; and (iii) accordingly, management has not provided any amounts in the consolidated financial statements for unfavorable outcomes, if any. Legal defense costs are expensed as incurred.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Income Tax Expense (Benefit)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We account for income taxes in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes. Under this method, deferred income taxes are determined based on the estimated future tax effects of differences between the financial statement and tax basis of assets and liabilities given the provisions of enacted tax laws. Deferred income tax provisions and benefits are based on changes to the assets or liabilities from year to year. In providing for deferred taxes, we consider tax regulations of the jurisdictions in which we operate, estimates of future taxable income, and available tax planning strategies. If tax regulations, operating results, or the ability to implement tax-planning strategies</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> vary</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, adjustments to the carrying value of the deferred tax assets and liabilities may be required. Valuation allowances are based on the &#x201C;more likely than not&#x201D; criteria of ASC 740.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The accounting for uncertain tax positions guidance under ASC 740 requires that we recognize the financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more likely than not sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">likely</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">than</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">not threshold, the amount recognized in the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> is the largest benefit that has a greater than 50 percent likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. We recognize interest and penalties on uncertain tax positions as a component of income tax expense. If our assessment of whether a tax position meets or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">does not </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">meet the more</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">likely</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">than</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">not threshold were to change, adjustments to income tax benefits may be required.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Results of Operations</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The following is our analysis of the results of operations for the periods covered by our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. This analysis should be read in conjunction with our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, including the related notes to the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. A detailed discussion of our accounting policies and procedures is set forth in the applicable sections of this analysis. Other accounting policies are contained in Note&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to the consolidated financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our chief operating decision maker, the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer, manages, assesses performance and allocates resources for our businesses based upon separate financial information for each of our operating segments (see Note 6 to our Consolidated Financial Statements for further information). In identifying the reportable segments, we also considered the nature of the services provided by our operating segments and other relevant factors. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Senior Care does not meet the quantitative thresholds for a reportable segment, however management believes that information about the segment should be separately disclosed as it is useful to the readers of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During 2016, management realigned its reporting structure by integrating the Quizzle operations into the Banking segment</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">revised the strategy of our Quizzle </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">operations</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to focus its technology resources primarily on enhancing the user experience of the products and services provided by the Banking segment through greater personalization. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">egment results reported for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">all periods since the acquisition of Quizzle in 2015 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">have been revised to reflect such change.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our operations in China were previously presented as a discontinued operation</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> as we were marketing them for sale. During the first half of 2016 we could not come to terms with the potential buyers of the business, negotiations ended</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and the plan to sell the business was abandoned. It was then determined to start the process of winding down and closing the operations in China, a process which, based on local requirements and regulations, is not expected to be completed until 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The operations of China are now included in our continuing operations for all periods presented. </font>

The Company&#x2019;s presentation of Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Credit Cards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue increased $73.0 million (30.2 %) for the year ended December 31, 2016 compared with 2015. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Approximately $29.1 million of the revenue growth came from NextAdvisor, which was acquired in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> June 2016. Excluding the impact of the acquisition, consumer inquiry revenue from our owned and operated sites grew by $40.2 million (23.4%). About 65% of consumer inquiry revenue growth resulted from higher pricing and sales conversion with the remaining from increased consumer volume. Other revenue, which is largely comprised of revenue generated through third-party affiliates, increased approximately 5.3%. Affiliate revenues yield substantially lower margins compared to revenues from owned and operated sites.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA increased $4.0 million (3.5%) due to increased revenues. Expenses increased primarily due to the inclusion of NextAdvisor, since its acquisition in June 2016, and higher paid marketing expense. Cost of revenue increased $57.4 million, mainly due to increased paid marketing expense and affiliate revenue share payments. Sales and marketing expense increased by $812,000. Product development cost increased by $4.9 million primarily due to higher compensation and incentive expense. General and administrative expenses were $5.9 million higher, mainly attributed to higher employee compensation and incentive expenses, increased consulting costs and higher facility and other costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Banking</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue decreased $8.2 million (7.5%) for the year ended December 31, 2016 compared with 2015. Of the total revenue decrease, consumer inquiry revenues generated through our rate tables decreased by $1.9 million (2.7%) as growth in mortgage and other products was offset by lower advertiser demand in our deposit vertical compared to prior year. Overall unit pricing was 19.4% lower due to our year-long efforts to align the price of each click with the value received by the advertiser, offset by a 20.8% increase in volume due to growth in our mortgage vertical. Other revenue, primarily from sold advertising impressions, was down approximately $6.3 million versus 2015. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA decreased $8.9 million (26.9%), primarily due to the decrease in revenues. Expenses included in Adjusted EBITDA increased $668,000 from the prior year. Cost of revenue decreased $633,000, primarily due to lower partner revenue share payments and paid marketing expense. Sales and marketing expenses increased $1.9 million, primarily due to increased compensation, benefits and incentive compensation, and increased information technology spending. Product development costs decreased by $43,000. General and administrative expenses were $597,000 lower due primarily to information technology and facility costs, partially offset by increased compensation, benefits and incentive compensation expense. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior Care</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenues decreased $375,000 (1.6%) for the year ended December 31, 2016 compared with 2015. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior housing referral revenue grew $1.3 million (7%) due to an increase in the number of move-ins and the average referral fee per move-in, despite losing our largest senior housing client in January 2016. The communities </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">lost with that client&#x2019;s departure </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">were more than replaced in our directory</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of providers</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, but by smaller, lower-converting senior housing providers. In the latter part of 2016 we conducted a pilot program with a small number of communities for this large senior housing client, and at year-end we won back a significant chunk of their business. In-home care referral revenue grew $289,000 with the Company&#x2019;s launch of its new home care cost-per-lead business in the summer of 2016. Subscription revenue declined $889,000 (36%) as senior housing clients were converted to referral contracts and in-home care clients were converted to cost-per-lead agreements. The loss of our largest senior housing client also adversely impacted subscription revenue. Advertising revenue was down $1.1 million (58%) following a decision to de-emphasize low margin pharmaceutical ad campaigns starting in 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA increased $594,000 primarily due to a $1.5 million decrease in cost of revenue related to lower paid marketing expense. Sales and Marketing expense increased $585,000 primarily due to compensation, benefits and incentive compensation. Product development increased $108,000 and general and administrative expenses decreased $243,000. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Other</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The Other segment includes general corporate expenses and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">intra-segment </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">eliminations. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2016 compared with 2015 decreased $1.4 million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> excluding China</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, while Adjusted EBITDA </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">excluding China operations</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, which are being wound down, decreased $8.0 million.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> The revenue decrease is attributed primarily to higher </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">intra-segment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> revenue eliminations. The decrease in Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$3.5 million in </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">compensation, benefits and incentive compensation expense, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$2.3 million in increased </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">consulting</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> costs</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> $1.7 million higher</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> accounting and other professional fees</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, and higher facility and information technology costs</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Total revenue increased 5.7% to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$372.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$352.1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million for the years ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">This increase is primarily due to higher consumer inquiry revenue on our owned and operated websites, partially offset by lower third-party affiliate, display and print revenues. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenues from our Credit Cards segment increased $15.0 million or 6.6% to $241.9 million in 2015 compared to 2014. Within the Banking segment, total revenue of $109.7 million in 2015 was 7.4% lower as compared to 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior Care revenues grew $13.6 million to $23.9 million in 2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> compared to a partial year of results after the business was acquired in May 2014. Other revenues increased $163,000, representing primarily lower intra-segment revenue eliminations. See our segment results discussion for more information. </font>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Credit Cards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue increased $15.0 million (6.6%) for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared with 2014. Of the total revenue growth, consumer inquiry revenues from our owned and operated sites grew by $48.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million (3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">%)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> About 5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">% of consumer inquiry revenue growth came from higher inquiry volume with the remaining increase through better monetization. Inquiry volume was partially driven by the April 2015 mobile respons</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">iv</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">e redesign of our creditcards.com site. Monetization growth was partly driven by higher advertising and marketing spend by credit card issuers through our owned and operated sites. However, overall revenue growth was negatively impacted by lower affiliate revenues. During the year, certain issuers and third party affiliates shifted their monetization links to other competing networks. Affiliate revenues yield substantially lower margins compared to revenues from owned and operated sites.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA increased $21.4 million (23.2%) due to a combination of increased revenues and a $6.4 million decrease in expenses included in Adjusted EBITDA. The decrease in expenses was primarily due to a</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">n</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> $1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million decrease in cost of revenue, mainly related to lower affiliate revenue share payments. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Sales and marketing expense </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">de</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">creased by $84,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. Product development cost increased by $1.9 million primarily due to higher compensation and incentive expense, increased professional fees and other costs. General and administrative expenses were $3.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million higher, mainly attributed to higher employee compensation and incentive expenses, increased consulting costs and higher travel, facility and other costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Banking</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenue </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">de</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">creased $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">8.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million (</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">%) for the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> compared with 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Consumer inquiry revenues generated through our rate tables decreased by $5.5 million (7.7%) primarily due to lower advertiser demand on our mortgage and deposit tables which resulted in a fewer consumer inquiries and lower monetization. This lower demand also impacted display revenue as many of the largest display advertisers on the Bankrate network also participate on our rate tables. As a result, other revenue, primarily from sold advertising impressions, was down approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million versus 2014.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> 2015 results include the results of Quizzle, which we acquired in 2015. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA decreased $1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million (26.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">%), primarily due to decreased revenues. Expenses included in Adjusted EBITDA </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">creased $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> from the prior year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and include the expenses of Quizzle, acquired in 2015. Cost of revenue decreased </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million, mainly related to lower partner revenue share payments. Sales and marketing expenses were $338,000 lower, primarily due to $274,000 lower sales commissions. Product development costs increased by $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.4 million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, due </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">primarily to higher employee compensation and benefits expense</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and outside contract labor costs. General and administrative expenses were $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.7 million higher due primarily to employee compensation and benefit </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">expense, information technology expenses</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and facility costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior Care</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revenues increased $13.6 million (131.6%) for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared with 2014 due partially to a full year of operations during 2015 after the mid-2014 acquisition of Caring and the acquisition of Senior Homes during 2015. In addition, the number of senior living communities contracted on a referral fee basis increased 50%, leading to a higher number of move-ins on an annualized basis, and the average referral fee increased by 18%. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA increased $3.0 million primarily due to revenue growth as expenses included in Adjusted EBITDA increased approximately $10.1 million, primarily due to a full year of operations and the acquisition of Senior Homes</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared with 2014 increased $163,000 due to primarily to lower intra-segment eliminations of segment revenue sharing. Adjusted EBITDA decreased by $3.3 million, due to higher corporate expenses.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Our principal ongoing source of operating liquidity is the cash generated by our business operations. We consider all highly liquid investments </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and debt investments </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">purchased with an original maturity of less than three months to be cash equivalents.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Our primary uses of cash have been to fund our working capital and capital expenditure needs, fund acquisitions,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> repurchase shares of our common stock</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and service our debt obligations. 			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Interest Rate Risk </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We maintain or may maintain </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">a portfolio of investments including bank deposits, U.S. Treasury</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> securities</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, U.S. Government Agency securities, municipal securities, corporate debt se</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">curities and money market funds.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s investment objectives, in order of priority, are 1) to preserve capital, 2) to maintain liquidity, and 3) to obtain a fair rate of return. In addition to other restrictions based on credit quality, the maximum maturity date for each investment is 24 months and the weighted average maturity of the portfolio may not exceed 12 months</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">None of our outstanding debt as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> was subject to variable interest rates as we did not have an outstanding balance for borrowed money under our Revolving Credit Facility as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. Interest under </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> Revolving Credit Facility accrues at variable rates based, at our option, on the alternate base rate (as defined in the Revolving Credit Facility) plus a margin of 3.00% or at the adjusted LIBO rate (as defined in the Revolving Credit Facility) plus a margin of 2.00%. Our fixed interest rate debt includes $300</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Senior Notes in aggregate principal amount.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Exchange Rate Sensitivity </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Our exposure to exchange rate risk is primarily that of a net receiver of currencies other than the U</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">S</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> dollar</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, primarily British Pound Sterling</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. Accordingly, changes in exchange rates, and in particular a strengthening of the U.S. dollar, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">can</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> affect the Company's net sales and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">income from operations</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> as expressed in U.S. dollars. Additionally, we have not engaged in any derivative or hedging transactions to date.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> During the year ended December 31, 2016, non-U.S. revenues were less than 1% of our total revenue. We estimate that a hypothetical 10% change (increase or decrease) in exchange rates would not have a material impact to our consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Garamond;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Bankrate, Inc. (a Delaware corporation) and subsidiaries (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) as of December 31, 2016 and 2015, and the related consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss), changes in stockholders&#x2019; equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2016. These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#x2019;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Garamond;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Garamond;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Bankrate, Inc. and subsidiaries as of December 31, 2016 and 2015, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2016 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">11</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>
