		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During the second quarter 2016, management noted that the operating results of its Banking reporting unit had begun to track below plan, primarily due to macroeconomic trends impacting its deposit and display advertising businesses. This triggering event resulted in impairment testing as of June 30, 2016. It was concluded that the reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill was impaired and we recorded a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$25.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million impairment of its goodwill in the second quarter 2016, determined using the income and market approaches. The Banking reporting unit was tested for impairment again during our annual assessment and it was concluded that no </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">further </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">impairment had occurred. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During 2016, management revised the strategy of its Quizzle reporting unit to focus its technology resources primarily on enhancing the user experience of the products and services provided by the Banking segment through greater personalization, and realigned its management reporting structure by integrating the Quizzle operations and reporting unit into the Banking reporting unit. Management determined that the revised strategy, reporting structure</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> change in the estimated useful life of Quizzle&#x2019;s developed technology intangible asset and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the performance of initiatives utilizing Quizzle resources, each represented triggering events for impairment testing at the pre-realigned Quizzle reporting unit. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">As a result, we completed Step 1 analysis of goodwill, which indicated that the fair value was lower than the reporting unit&#x2019;s carrying value. In accordance with ASC 350-20-35-18, management elected to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">record an estimated goodwill impairment of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$4.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">as of September 30, 2016, subject to completing our review and finalizing Step 2 of the analysis during the fourth quarter 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">D</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">uring the fourth quarter 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, we completed Step 2 of the analysis</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, record</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ing an</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">dditional </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">goodwill impairment of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$2.4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million for the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">pre-realigned Quizzle reporting unit </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for the year ended December 31, 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The impairment amount was determined using the income and market approaches, and was based on a number of factors including the estimated fair value of developed technology, trademarks and customer relationships</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (all valued using an income approach)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, as well as relevant market related data.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Additionally, i</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">t was determined that the intangible assets of our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">pre-realigned </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Quizzle business unit were impaired and we recorded</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> an intangible asset impairment of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$7.5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for the year ended December 31, 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company followed the guidance in ASC 350-20-35 and performed the annual impairment test of goodwill as of October 1, 2016. In performing that test, it was noted that the carrying value of the Senior Care reporting unit exceeded its fair value. As a result, Step 2 was required to be performed. The implied fair value of goodwill was determined in the same manner as the amount of goodwill recognized in a business combination. We have determined the fair value of the reporting unit using the income and market approaches. We also determined the fair value of developed technology, domain names and customer relationships, using relevant</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> market data. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">recorded </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">goodwill impairment of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$4.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million for the Senior Care reporting unit for the year ended December 31, 2016.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During 2015, it was determined that a triggering event had occurred in our former Insurance business unit. We recorded a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$35.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million charge for the impairment of goodwill within our Insurance segment resulting from the difference between the net book value of the business segment and the estimated fair value of the business. During the annual goodwill impairment testing, on October 1, 2015, we performed the assessment for all reporting units, including Step 2 testing for the Insurance business unit, and concluded that there was no impairment of goodwill including any further impairment of the Insurance business unit. During the fourth quarter 2015, the Insurance business was disposed and as such, the results of the business are presented as a discontinued operation for all periods presented.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">T</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">he chief operating decision</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> maker, the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">manages, assesses performance and allocates resources for the business based upon the separate financial information from the Company&#x2019;s operating segments. In identifying </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">its</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> reportable segments, the Company also considered the nature of the services provided by its operating segments and other relevant factors.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Senior Care does not meet the quantitative thresholds for a reportable segment, however management believes that information about the segment should be separately disclosed as it is useful to the readers of the financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In evaluating and assessing performance of the Company&#x2019;s operating segments, and when allocating resources to business units needed in accomplishing its strategic goals, the assets of the business units are not a primary consideration of the chief operating decision maker. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The reportable segments presented below represent the Company&#x2019;s operating segments for which separate financial information is available and utilized on a regular basis by its chief operating decision maker, the Company&#x2019;s chief executive officer, to assess performance and allocate resources. Management evaluates the operating results of each of the Company&#x2019;s operating segments based upon revenue and &#x201C;Adjusted EBITDA&#x201D;, which we define as income from continuing operations before depreciation and amortization; interest; income taxes; changes in fair value of contingent acquisition consideration; stock-based compensation and other items such as loss on extinguishment of debt, legal settlements, acquisition, disposition and related expenses; restructuring charges; any impairment charges; NextAdvisor contingent</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> deferred compensation </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for the acquisition; costs related to the Restatement, the Internal Review, the SEC and DOJ investigations and related litigation and indemnification obligations; purchase accounting adjustments; and our operations in China as we are winding down and ceasing its operations. The Company&#x2019;s presentation of Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, may not be comparable to similarly titled m</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">easures used by other companies</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"></font>

				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:12.48%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #auto;;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap">297,000&nbsp;
				</td>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">__________</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent: -18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">A</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%;font-size: 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">The carrying amount of long term debt is net of original issue discount and deferred financing fees</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We make</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> recurring fair value measurements of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> contingent acquisition consideration using Level 3 unobservable inputs. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> recognize the fair value of contingent acquisition consideration based on its estimated fair value at the date of acquisition using discounted cash flows</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, Monte Carlo simulations or probability weighted-expected return model</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. S</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">ubsequent adjustments to the fair value are due to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">either </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the passage of time as we approach the payment date or changes to management&#x2019;s estimates of the projected results of the acquired business. In determining the fair value of contingent acquisition consideration, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">we </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">review current results of the acquired business along with projected results for the remaining earnout period</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to calculate the expected contingent acquisition consideration to be paid using the agreed upon formula as laid out in the acquisition agreements. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The fair value of the contingent acquisition consideration liability </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">will be adjusted based on the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> change in fair value of contingent consideration resulting from the passage of time at the applicable discount rate</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, or changes in the forecasted results</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> as we approach the payment dates of the contingent consideration absent any significant changes in assumptions related to the valuation or the probability of payment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">In addition, we make recurring fair value measurement of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">a &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">contingent acquisition </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">deferred compensation liability </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">using Level 3 unobservable inputs. We recognize the fair value based on its estimated fair value at the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">beginning period </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">date using discounted cash flows, Monte Carlo simulations or probability weighted-expected return model</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. S</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">ubsequent adjustments to the fair value are due to the passage of time as we approach the payment date or changes to management&#x2019;s estimates of the projected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">performance target</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. In determining the fair value, we review current results along with projected results for the remaining earnout period to calculate the expected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">contingent acquisition deferred compensation </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">to be paid using the agreed upon formula as laid out in the acquisition agreement. The fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">contingent acquisition deferred compensation liability </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">will be adjusted based on the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">change in fair value resulting from the passage of time at the applicable discount rate</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, or changes in the forecasted results</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> as we approach the payment dates of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">contingent acquisition deferred compensation </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">absent any significant changes in assumptions related to the valuation or the probability of payment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The unobservable inputs used in determining the fair value of contingent acquisition consideration for earnout periods not yet completed include discount factors of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">14%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> based on our weighted average cost of capital and projected results of the acquired businesses. In addition, we consider the cost of debt to be a significant input in the valuation of the fair value of the contingent acquisition deferred compensation and certain contin</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">ent acquisition consideration liabilities. We used </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> percent as our cost of debt in these valuations as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. The fair value calculated as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> is subject to sensitivity as it relates to the projected results of the acquired businesses, which are uncertain in nature. Each calculation is based on a separate formula and results that differ from our projections could impact the fair value significantly.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The following tables present</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> fair value measurements of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> contingent acquisition consideration</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">contingent acquisition deferred compensation</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">assets of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> non-qualified deferred compensation plan</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> using the fair value hierarchy. </font>

partially offset by </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">a decrease in the fair value</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">25</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">5,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> due to the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">chang</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">e</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> certain estimates of the projected results</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> stock-based compensation program is a long-term retention program that is intended to attract, retain and provide incentives for directors, officers and employees in the form of non-qualified stock options, restricted stock and performance</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">-</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">based restricted shares</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> or units</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">typically </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">settle stock-based awards with treasury shares. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">August</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> 2015, the Company</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;s stockholders approved </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the 2015 Equity Compensation Plan (the &#x201C;2015 Plan&#x201D;), replacing the former 2011 Equity Compensation Plan (the &#x201C;2011 Plan&#x201D;), to grant stock-based awards for up to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">hares of our common stock. Under the 2015 Plan, the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Compensation Committee of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Board of Directors or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">another Committee or delegate designated by the Board of Directors or</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Compensation Committee </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">has the sole authority to determine who receives such grants, the type, size and timing of such grants, and to specify the terms of</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> such awards</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The purpose of the 2015 Plan is to attract and retain officers, employees and non-employees, to provide such persons incentives and rewards and to align the participants&#x2019; economic interests with that of our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">stockholders. As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">hares were available for future issuance under the 2015 plan.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During the year ended December 31, 2016, there were no significant modifications to stock options or stock awards. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">During the year ended December 31, 2015, the Company modified certain </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">stock options and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">stock awards </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">for approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">40 </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">individuals,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> granted in 2013, 2014 and 2015, related to the sale of its Insurance business</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and its restructuring initiatives</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. The modification resulted in an acceleration of the vesting periods </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">of restricted and performance-based stock awards </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and an extension of the exercise period</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of the stock options</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. These modifications resulted in an additional expense of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$9.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million for t</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">he year ended December 31, 2015, of which, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$6.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million is recorded as a component of the net loss from discontinued operation and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$3.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million is recorded as a component of restructuring expense.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During 2016, performance-based restricted stock units were awarded that vest based upon a performance factor, which is equal to a measure of the Company&#x2019;s profitability over a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> year period and multiplied by a total shareholder return factor achieved by the Company relative to a determined peer group, with </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> vesting on the determination date, which will be the later of (i) the date on which the audit of the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> for its fiscal year 2017 is completed and (ii) the date on which the final calculation of the relative total shareholder return factor is made by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors; and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> on the third anniversary of the grant date. The granted amount represents the target amount of performance-based restricted stock units to be awarded. The amount awarded is determined based on the Company&#x2019;s financial performance metric, Adjusted EBITDA. The total number of performance-based restricted stock units earned based on the financial performance metric can range from </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">150%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of the target amount. The total shareholder return factor could further adjust the number of performance-based restricted stock units earned by a maximum increase or decrease of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">25%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Stock-based compensation expense related to the performance-based restricted stock units for the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">year ended</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, there was unrecognized compensation expense related to non-vested performance-based restricted stock units of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, net of forfeitures, which is expected to be recognized over an estimated weighted average period of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The grant date fair value of performance-based restricted stock units incorporates a total-stockholders return metric, which is estimated using a Monte Carlo simulation model to estimate the Company&#x2019;s ranking relative to an applicable stock index of peers. The weighted average assumptions used in the Monte Carlo simulation model to calculate the fair value of the Company&#x2019;s performance-based restricted stock unit awards are outlined below.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Stock Options</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We use the Black-Scholes option pricing model to determine the fair value of our stock options. The determination of the fair value of the awards on the date of grant using an option-pricing model is affected by the price of our common stock, as well as assumptions regarding a number of complex and subjective variables</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, and is considered a Level 3 unobservable input</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">. These variables include expected stock price volatility over the term of the awards, actual and projected employee stock option exercise behaviors, risk-free interest rates, expected dividends and the estimated forfeiture rate. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We estimated the expected term of outstanding stock options by considering the vesting term and the contractual term of the option, as well as the historical option exercise behavior of employees, as illustrated in ASC&nbsp;718, Compensation&#x2014;Stock Compensation. The estimated volatility of our common stock is determined based on facts and circumstances at the time of the grant, along with the historical trading volatility of our stock.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For stock option grants issued prior to 2014, we used the simplified method to estimate the expected term for employee stock option grants and we previously estimated the volatility of our common stock by using an average of historical stock price volatility of publicly traded entities that are considered peers to Bankrate </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in accordance with ASC&nbsp;718. We based the risk-free interest rate used in the option pricing model on U.S.&nbsp;Treasury constant maturity issues having remaining terms similar to the expected terms of the options. We do not anticipate paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future and therefore use an expected dividend yield of zero in the option pricing model. We are required to estimate forfeitures at the time of grant and revise those estimates in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. We use historical data to estimate pre-vesting option forfeitures and record share-based compensation expense only for those awards that are expected to vest. All share-based payment awards are </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">recognized </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods, which is generally the vesting period. During the fourth quarter of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, we evaluated our forfeiture rate based on historical experience and updated the forfeiture rate from </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">12</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. If factors change and we employ different assumptions for estimating share-based compensation expense in future periods or if we decide to use a different valuation model, the future periods may differ significantly from what we have recorded in the current period and could materially affect our operating income, net income and net income per share. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Stock options </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">granted contained a contractual term of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">seven year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">s. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Stock option activity </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and grants outstanding were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">as follows for the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">years ended</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> and as of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> December 31: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">800,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font 		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Pursuant to the income tax provisions of ASC 718, we follow the &#x201C;long-haul method&#x201D; of computing our hypothetical additional paid-in capital, or APIC, pool. Approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">88</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> stock options vested during the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> The intrinsic value of stock options exercised during the years ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">83,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">nd </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">8.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">million, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">As of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">400,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of total unrecognized compensation costs, net of forfeitures, related to non-vested stock option awards is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">years.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Legal Proceedings</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">From time to time, the Company is party to litigation and regulatory matters and claims. The Company expenses legal fees as incurred. The Company records a provision for contingent losses when it is both probable that a liability will be incurred and the amount or range of the loss can be reasonably estimated. The results of complex proceedings and reviews are difficult to predict and the Company&#x2019;s view of these matters may change in the future as events related thereto unfold. Except as otherwise stated, we have concluded that we cannot estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss, including reasonably possible losses in excess of amounts already accrued, for each matter disclosed below. An unfavorable outcome to any legal or regulatory matter, if material, could have an adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s operations or its financial position, liq</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">uidity or results of operations</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">BanxCorp Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In July 2007, BanxCorp, an online publisher of rate information provided by financial institutions with respect to various financial products, filed suit against the Company in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey alleging violations of Federal and New Jersey State antitrust laws, including the Sherman Act and the Clayton Act. BanxCorp has alleged that it has been injured as a result of monopolistic and otherwise anticompetitive conduct on the part of the Company and is seeking approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$180</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in compensatory damages, treble damages, and attorneys' fees and costs. In October 2012, BanxCorp filed a Seventh Amended Complaint, alleging violations of Section 2 of the Sherman Act, Section 7 of the Clayton Act and parallel provisions of New Jersey antitrust laws, and dropping its claims under Section 1 of the Sherman Act. Discovery closed on December 21, 2012 and both parties filed motions in the first quarter of 2013 seeking summary judgment that are pending before the court. The Company will continue to vigorously defend this lawsuit. The Company cannot presently estimate the amount of loss, if any, that would result from an adverse resolution of this matter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Securities Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In October 2014, a putative class action lawsuit was brought in federal court in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida against the Company, certain of its current and former officers and directors, and other defendants, which is captioned The City of Los Angeles v. Bankrate, Inc., et al., No. 14-CV-81323-DMM. On November 23, 2015, the District Court dismissed an amended complaint in its entirety without prejudice for failing to adequately plead material misrepresentations or omissions, scienter, or loss causation and damages. On December 8, 2015, Lead Plaintiff filed a Second Amended Complaint alleging that the Company&#x2019;s 2012, 2013, and first half of 2014 financial statements improperly recognized revenues and expenses and therefore were materially false and misleading and caused damages. Plaintiffs sought relief (including damages and rescission or rescissionary damages) under the Securities Act of 1933 based on a March 2014 secondary offering and under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of a proposed class consisting of all persons, other than the defendants, who purchased the Company&#x2019;s securities between August 1, 2012 and October 9, 2014, inclusive. On May 17, 2016, the Company announced a proposed agreement, subject to Court approval, to settle this private securities class action against all defendants. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Under the settlement,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Bankrate </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">agreed to pay</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">a total of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$20</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in cash to a Settlement Fund to resolve all claims asserted on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bankrate stock between October 27, 2011 and October 9, 2014. The settlement further provide</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">d</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> that Bankrate denies all claims of wrongdoing or liability. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The court granted final approval of the settlement on February 6, 2017.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company accrued the settlement amount as of June 30, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and funded approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$6.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million to the settlement fund</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$13.8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million of the settlement fund has been</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> funded from insurance proceeds</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">DOJ Investigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">As previously reported, the DOJ has informed the Company that it is investigating the matters that were the subject of the SEC investigation settled by the Company in 2015. It is not possible to predict when the DOJ investigation will be completed, the final outcome of the investigation, and what if any actions may be taken by the DOJ.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">CFPB Investigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company and certain of its employees have received Civil Investigative Demands (CIDs) from the CFPB to produce certain documents and answer questions relating to the Company&#x2019;s quality control process for its online mortgage rate tables. The Company has cooperated in responding to the CIDs. In late 2015, the Company received a communication from the CFPB inviting the Company to respond to the CFPB&#x2019;s identified issues in the form of a Notice of Opportunity to Respond and Advise during which the CFPB identified potential claims it might bring against the Company. In early 2016, the Company submitted a response that it believes addressed the CFPB&#x2019;s issues with respect to the Company&#x2019;s online mortgage rate tables and its quality control processes. We are unable to predict when the CFPB investigation will be completed or the final outcome of the investigation, and cannot presently estimate the amount of loss, if any, that would result from an adverse resolution of this matter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In addition to the above, we are also involved in other litigation and regulatory matters and claims that arise in the ordinary course of business and although we cannot be certain of the outcome of any such litigation or claims, nor the amount of damages and exposure that we could incur, we currently believe that the final disposition of such matters will not have a material effect on our business, financial position, results of operations or cash flow. Regardless of the outcome, litigation and regulatory matters can have an adverse impact on us because of investigative, defense or settlement costs, diversion of management resources and other factors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

The lease incentives are reflected as components of other current liabilities and other liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">We consider lease renewals in the useful life of our leasehold improvements when such renewals are reasonably assured. We take these provisions into account when calculating minimum aggregate rental commitments under non-cancelable operating leases. </font>

In total, the Company paid </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$374,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> in consent fees to holders of the Senior Notes in connection with the execution and effectiveness of the Third Supplemental Indenture.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our Senior Notes Indenture</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> generally permit us to apply the net cash proceeds of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$130.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million from the sale of our Insurance business to prepay outstanding debt and/or invest in assets useful to our business, in each case, within 365 days of our receipt of such net cash proceeds (subject, in the case of any investment, to a further 180-day extension under certain circumstances). If we do not apply such net cash proceeds in the manner and within the time period described above and the amount of unapplied net cash proceeds exceeds </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$10.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, we will be required to offer to purchase a portion of our outstanding Senior Notes using those unapplied net cash proceeds at an offer price equal to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of the principal amount of the Senior Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, up to but not including, the date of purchase. As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Dec</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ember 3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">it was determined that there were less than $10.0 million in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">unused net cash proceeds from the sale of our Insurance business</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> that had not been applied as described above.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Revolving Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">In </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">August 2013, the Company entered into a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">$70.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> million revolving facility (&#x201C;Revolving Credit Facility&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> matur</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">May 17, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">among the Company, as borrower, certain subsidiaries of the Company, as guarantors (the &#x201C;Guarantors&#x201D;), the lenders party thereto (the &#x201C;Lenders&#x201D;), Royal Bank of Canada, as administrative agent, and the other parties thereto. The proceeds of any loans made under the Revolving Credit Facility can be used for ongoing working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes, including the financing of capital expenditures and acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility bear interest at a rate per annum equal to, at the Company&#x2019;s option, either (i)&nbsp;an alternate base rate (as defined in the Revolving Credit Facility) or (ii)&nbsp;an adjusted LIBO rate (as defined in the Revolving Credit Facility), each calculated in a customary manner, plus applicable margin. The applicable margin is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">3.00%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;per annum with respect to alternate base rate loans and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2.00%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;per annum with respect to adjusted LIBO rate loans. In addition to paying interest on the outstanding principal amount of borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility, the Company must pay a commitment fee to the Lenders in respect of their average daily unused amount of revolving commitments at a rate that ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0.375%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">0.500%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> per annum depending on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated total leverage ratio. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">These commitment fees are recorded in interest expense. T</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">he Company may voluntarily prepay loans under the Revolving Credit Facility at any time without premium or penalty (subject to customary &#x201C;breakage&#x201D; fees in the case of Eurodollar rate loans).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">The </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> contains customary affirmative and negative covenants (including, but not limited to, covenants restricting the payment of dividends and incurrence of additional indebtedness) and events of default and requires the Company to comply with a maximum consolidated total leverage ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">4.00</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">:1.00 as of the last day of any</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">quarter only if the aggregate amount (without duplication) of letters of credit (other than letters of credit that are issued and not drawn to the extent such letters of credit are cash collateralized) and loans outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility exceed, on a pro forma basis, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">30%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> of the total revolving commitments of all Lenders at such time. The Company was in compliance with all required covenants as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">All obligations under the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> are guaranteed by the Guarantors and are secured, subject to certain exceptions, by first priority liens on the assets of the Company and the Guarantors. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">NOTE 1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;"> &#x2013; ACQUISITIONS</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">June 17, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, we completed the acquisition of certain assets of Next Advisor, Inc. (the &#x201C;Acquired NextAdvisor Business&#x201D;), an online source of research and reviews of credit cards, personal finance and internet services. This acquisition was made to accelerate our business, broaden our reach and increase ways to engage consumers looking for credit cards. The results of operations of the Acquired NextAdvisor Business are being reported in our Credit Cards segment and are included in our consolidated results from the acquisition date. The acquisition is accounted for as a business combination</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> acquisition accounting is preliminary and subject to change as third party valuations are not finalized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company paid </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$63.4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million at closing, recorded </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$37.3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million of deferred contingent consideration, and placed </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$11.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million into escrow as a deferred payment and to serve as recourse for indemnity obligations. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">An additional </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$1.3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million was paid to the seller subsequent to the closing date related to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">net working capital adjustments.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The deferred payment is recorded in other </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">current </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">assets and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> be</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> amortized into compensation expense over the period earned. As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Dec</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ember 3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$4.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million was paid from escrow </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">to the seller. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The transaction called for cash consideration as well as a series of contingent payments based on the achievement of Adjusted EBITDA targets. We have estimated contingent payments, which are classified as purchase consideration if made or due to the seller and as compensation if made to current employees. As part of the purchase price, the Company recorded a $37.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million liability on the date of acquisition for the deferred contingent consideration due to seller based upon the net present value of the Company&#x2019;s estimate of the future payments. Subsequent measurements are made using the same methodology. This fair value measurement represents a Level 3 measurement as it is based on significant inputs not observable in the market. Significant judgment is employed in determining the appropriateness of these assumptions as of the acquisition date.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> This contingent consideration has a maximum potential earnout of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$13</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1 million if all related targets are achieved, and is payable in either cash or shares of the Company&#x2019;s stock. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Subsequent changes to the fair value of the contingent acquisition consideration are recorded as changes in fair value of contingent acquisition consideration</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> see Note </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &#x2013; Fair Value Measurement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We recorded approximately $6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in goodwill, which reflects the adjustments necessary to allocate the purchase price to the fair value of the assets acquired and the liabilities assumed and represents the expected future economic benefits from future growth arising from the Acquired NextAdvisor Business&#x2019;s scale and expertise in driving traffic via sponsored content, benefits expected from using that expertise to drive traffic to other Bankrate-owned websites, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">future economic benefits arising from other assets acquired that could not be individually identified and separately recognized. We expect goodwill will be deductible for income tax purposes. The valuations used to determine the preliminary estimated fair value of the intangible assets and the resulting goodwill in the purchase price allocation principally use the discounted cash flow methodology and were made concurrent with the effective date of the acquisition. Intangible assets including trademarks and internet domain name, customer relationships, and the non-compete covenant were valued using the income approach, and the developed technology was valued using cost methodology. Approximately $30.0 million was recorded as intangible assets </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">with estimated weighted average useful lives of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> years</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">consisting of customer relationships for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$22.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, trademarks and internet domain name for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$6.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, non-compete covenant for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$1.4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million and developed technology for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$150,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The current assets and receivables acquired and the current liabilities assumed were valued at cost</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, which approximates fair value</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>

						<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font></p>
